n74179.head: ὀνόφυλλον
n74179.html:
ὀνόφυλλον, τό,

gloss on ὄνου πετάλειον ὀριγάνου, Sch. Nic. Th. 628.

n74180.head: ὀνοχειλές
n74180.html:
ὀνοχειλές, έος, τό,

Cretan bugloss, Echium parviflorum, Ps.-Dsc. 4.23 (whence restd. in Thphr. HP 7.10.3, for ὀνοκίχλης), Plin. HN 22.51 :—also ὀνό-χειλος, ἡ, Aët. 1.5, Paul.Aeg. 7.3 p.187 H.:

n74181.head: ὀνόχηλον
n74181.html:
ὀνόχηλον, τό, as if from χηλή,

assʼs hoof, Sch. Nic. Th. 838 (with v.l. -χειλον); cf. ὀνοκλεία.

n74182.head: ὄντα
n74182.html:
ὄντα, τά, neut. pl. part. of εἰμί (sum),

the things which actually exist, the present, opp. the past and future, E. Hel. 14 ; but also,

2 reality, truth, opp. that which is not, Pl. Sph. 263d ; actual objects, σκιὰς τῶν ὄντων Id. R. 532c, etc. ; v. εἰμί.

II that which one has, property, fortune (cf. οὐσία), D. 18.102.

n74183.head: ὀντοποιέω
n74183.html:
ὀντοποιέω,

make things to be, Dam. Pr. 65.

n74184.head: ὀντότης
n74184.html:
ὀντότης, ητος, ἡ,

reality, Alex.Aphr. in Metaph. 641.27, Eustr. in EN 13.7.

n74185.head: ὄντως
n74185.html:
ὄντως, Adv. part. of εἰμί

(sum), really, actually, verily, with Verbs, E. HF 610, Ion 223 (lyr.), IA [1622], Ar. Nu. 86, Pl. 286, 289, Herod. 4.65, etc.; ὄντως τε καὶ ἀληθῶς really and truly, Pl. Sph. 263d ; ὄ. φιλοσοφεῖν Epicur. Fr. 220 ; opp. to ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν, Pl. Lg. 656e ; to εἰκότως, Antipho 2.2.10 and 4.10 : in Pl. with the part. ὤν, οὖσα, ὄν, to imply real existence, Phdr. 247c, 247e, R. 597d : also with Nouns, τὰ ὄντως ἀγαθά Id. Phdr. 260a; ὅ γε ὄντως φιλομαθής Id. R. 490a ; ὄντως ἑταίρας Antiph. 212.6, cf. Men. 367, etc.: not used by Th. or Arist., nor in Ion. (ἐόντως is not found) ; more freq in the later dialogues of Pl. than in the earlier.

n74186.head: ὅνυ
n74186.html:
ὅνυ,

Arc. and Cypr. for ὅδε, declined like ὁ with addition of -νυ, nom. sg. masc. ὅνυ Inscr.Cypr. 141 H., acc. τόνυ ib. 140H., dat. τῷνυ Schwyzer 664.11 (Orchom. Arc., iv B. C.), acc. pl. neut. τάνυ IG 5(2).3.14 (Tegea, iv B. C.), gen. τῶννυ SIG 306.59 (ibid., iv B. C.), IG 5(2).262.23 (Mantinea, v B. C.), dat. pl. fem. ταῖννυ SIG 306.30 ; also, with -νυν for -νυ, acc. sg. fem. τάννυν, acc. pl. masc. τόσνυν, ib. 559.48, 49 (Megalopolis, found at Magn. Mae., iii B. C.).

n74187.head: ὀνύδιν
n74187.html:
ὀνύδιν, τό,

= ὀνάριον, PGoodsp.Cair. 15.16 (iv A. D.).

n74188.head: ὄνυμα
n74188.html: ὄνυμα, ὀνυμάζω, ὀνυμαίνω, ὀνυμαστός, Aeol. and Dor. for ὀνομ-.

n74189.head: ὄνυξ
n74189.html:
ὄνυξ, ῠχος, ὁ, Hom. only in Ep. dat. pl. ὀνύχεσσι, and always of the eagle,

talons, claws, Il. 8.248, al. ; so of the falcon, Hes. Op. 204, 205, Ar. Av. 1180 ; so of beasts of prey, Pi. N. 4.63, Hdt. 3.108 ; of the crocodile, Id. 2.68 ; of the Sphinx, E. El. 471 (lyr.); of human beings, nail, Hes. Sc. 266, Hdt. 4.64, etc.; τοὺς ὄνυχας τῶν δακτύλων Ar. Av. 8 ; of horses and oxen, hoof, X. Eq. 1.3, AP 9.64 (Asclep. or Arch.): Arist. speaks of the hoof (ὁπλή) as homologous to the nail or claw (ὄνυξ), HA 486b20, PA 690a9: metaph., πρὸς ὀξύν γʼ ὄ. πετραίου λίθου E. Cyc. 401 codd. (leg. στόνυχα) :—Special phrases :

1 εἰς ἄκρους τοὺς ὄ. ἀφίκετο (sc. ὁ οἶνος) warmed me to my fingers’ ends, ib. 159; so ἐκ κορυφῆς εἰς ἄκρους ὄ. AP 9.709 (Phil.), cf. 12.93 (Rhian.) ; so also ἐξ ὀνύχων from the fingers’ ends, ib. 5.13 (Rufin.), Plu. Lib.educ. 2.3c ; but ἐξ ἁπαλῶν ὀ. from childhood, Horaceʼs de tenero ungui, AP 5.128 (Autom.).

2 ὄνυχας ἐπʼ ἄκρους στάς on tiptoe, E. El. 840 ; ἐπʼ ἄκρων ἐβάδιζε τῶν ὀ. Macho ap. Ath. 8.349b.

3 ὅταν ἐν ὄνυχι ὁ πηλὸς γένηται, i. e. when the model reaches the nail stage, because the sculptor puts the finishing touches to the model with his nail, Polyclit. ap. Plu. QConv. 2.636c, cf. Plu. Profect. 2.86a ; so ἡ διʼ ὄνυχος δίαιτα a most careful, close life, Sanit. ib. 128e ; τὸν Λυσιακὸν χαρακτῆρα ἐκμέμακται εἰς ὄνυχα ad unguem expressit, D.H. Dem. 13 ; σύμπηξις εἰς ὄνυχα a nice fit, Gal. 2.737 ; τὰς γωνίας ἐπʼ ὄνυχος συμβεβλημένας ἔχειν Ph. Bel. 66.37 ; πρὸς ὄνυχα τὴν προσκαρτέρησιν ποιεῖσθαι Phld. Rh. 1.11 S.; cf. ὀνυχίζω III, ἐξονυχίζω.

4 ὀδοῦσι καὶ ὄνυξι καὶ πάσῃ μηχανῇ, i.e. in every possible way, Luc. DMort. 21[11].4.

5 ἐξ ὀνύχων λέοντα (sc. τεκμαίρεσθαι) to judge by the claws, i. e. by a slight but characteristic mark, Alc. 113, Apostol. 7.57.

II anything like a claw,

1 fluke of an anchor, Plu. Mul.virt. 2.247e.

2 an instrument fixed by a surgeon to his finger, Hp. Superf. 7, Gal. 19.107.

3 ὄ. σιδηροῦς tool used for scraping the ‘figs’ of the συκάμινος, Thphr. HP 4.2.1 (pl.) ; also for making incisions to extract gum of balsam, ib. 9.6.2 (pl.).

4 κλιμακίδοιν τοὺς ὄ., τῶν πλαισίων τοὺς ὄ., dub. sens. in IG 1(2).373.208, 212, cf. 372 E 10.

III anything like the nail:

1 the white part at the end of rose-petals by which they are attached to the stalk, Dsc. 1.99.

2 hypopyon, an accumulation of pus in the eye resembling a nail-paring, Aët. 7.30 tit. (pl.), Paul.Aeg. 3.22.23.

3 part of the liver, Ruf. Onom. 180, Sch. Nic. Th. 560.

4 veined gem, onyx, LXX Jb. 28.16, Aristeas 66, J. BJ 5.5.7 ; Σαρδῷος ὄ. sardonyx, Luc. Syr.D. 32 (cf. σαρδόνυξ) ; ὄ. σφραγίς IG 2(2).1388.86, cf. 12.282.128.

5 an aromatic substance, onycha, LXX Ex. 30.34, Damocr. ap. Gal. 13.226, Dsc. 2.8, POxy. 1142.4 (iii A. D.).

6 = ἀστράγαλος VII, Ps.-Dsc. 4.61.

7 operculum of the κογχύλιον, Dsc. 2.8, Gal. 13.320, Orib. 5.77.1, Paul.Aeg. 7.3 ; of the πορφύρα, Dsc. Eup. 2.92.

8 a shell-fish, supposed female of σωλήν, prob. Lithodomus, Xenocr. ap. Orib. 2.58.106 (pl.).

9 ὄνυχες θαλάσσιοι sea-weed, Ps.-Democr.Alch. p.42 B. (Cf. Lat. unguis, Skt. nakhás ‘nail’, etc.)

n74191.head: ὀνυχάλειμμα
n74191.html:
ὀνυχάλειμμα [ᾰ], ατος, τό,

ointment of ὄνυξ III.5, Hippiatr. 100.

n74192.head: ὀνυχιαῖος
n74192.html:
ὀνυχιαῖος, α, ον,

of a nailʼs breadth, Eust.ad D.P. Prooem. p.73.31 B.

n74193.head: ὀνυχίζω
n74193.html:
ὀνυχίζω,

pare the nails. in Med., Jul. Mis. 339b, Iamb. VP 28.154 : aor ὠνυχισάμην LXX 2 Ki. 19.24(25) :—Pass., ὠνυχισμένος with oneʼs nails pared, Cratin. 455.

II ὀ. ὄνυχας to have the hoof cloven, LXX Le. 11.7, al.

III examine with the nail, examine closely, Artem. 4 Prooem., Jul. Or. 5.162c : fut. ὀνυχιεῖ· ἐπιμελῶς ἐξετάσει, Hsch. :—Pass., ὀνυχίζεται, expld. by Phot. ἀκριβολογεῖται, Ar. Fr. 834.

IV overreach, ἐν τῇ συνηθείᾳ -ίζεσθαί φαμεν τὸν ἐπὶ βλάβῃ ὑπό τινος ἐξαπατηθέντα Artem. 1.22.

n74194.head: ὀνυχιμαῖος
n74194.html:
ὀνυχιμαῖος, α, ον,

of the size of nail-parings, diminutive, Com.Adesp. 879.

n74195.head: ὀνύχινος
n74195.html:
ὀνύχινος, η, ον, (ὄνυξ III.4)

made of onyx, IG 11(2).287 B 70 (Delos, iii B. C.), Posidon. 25 J., Plu. Ant. 58, etc.

2 like onyx, Plin. HN 15.55 ; esp. onyx-coloured, of garments, POxy. 114.6 (ii/iii A. D.), 1026.10 (v A. D.) ; πρόβατα PGen. 68.6 (iv A. D.).

II ὀνύχινον (sc. ἔλαιον), made of ὄνυξ III.5, Dsc. 1.54.2.

n74196.head: ὀνύχιον
n74196.html:
ὀνύχιον, τό,

Dim. of ὄνυξ 1, small claw, Arist. HA 503a29.

2 pigʼs trotters, Sammelb. 1941 (iv A. D.), PLond. 3.1259.37 (iv A. D.).

3 an eye-disease, = ὄνυξ III.2, PMed.Strassb. p.6 K.: pl., Aët. 7.30.

4 σκόρδων ὀνύχια cloves of garlic, Id. 11.11.

II (ὄνυξ III 4) a kind of onyx, Thphr. Lap. 31, LXX Ex. 28.20 : as Adj. ὀνύχιος (sc. λίθος), Suid.

corr.why: one of 153 typo fixes made in copy B in 2020 that the Logeion copy lacked; carried over on 23 Oct 2026

n74197.head: ὀνυχισμός
n74197.html:
ὀνυχισμός, ὁ,

paring of the nails, Str. 17.3.7.

n74198.head: ὀνυχιστήρ
n74198.html:
ὀνυχιστήρ, ῆρος, ὁ,

hoof, LXX Le. 11.3, al.

n74199.head: ὀνυχιστήριον
n74199.html:
ὀνυχιστήριον, τό,

nail-knife or scissors, Posidipp. 38 ; = unguicularium, Gloss.

n74200.head: ὀνυχίτης
n74200.html:
ὀνυχίτης [ῑ], ου, ὁ, (ὄνυξ III 4)

of the onyx kind, ὀ. λίθος Dsc. 5.74 :—also fem. ὀνῠχ-ῖτις λίθος, App. Mith. 115, cf. Plin. HN 34.103.

n74201.head: ὀνυχογραφέομαι
n74201.html:
ὀνυχογραφέομαι, Pass.,

to be scored with the nail, Hp. Epid. 6.6.4.

n74202.head: ὀνυχοειδής
n74202.html:
ὀνυχοειδής, ές,

like a nail, Dsc. 1.64.3.

n74203.head: ὀνυχόπαχος
n74203.html:
ὀνυχόπαχος, ον,

of the thickness of a finger-nail, Ps.-Democr.Alch. p.48 B.

n74205.head: ὀνυχοφόρος
n74205.html:
ὀνυχοφόρος, ον,

carrying the nails, of the last phalanx of the finger, Cat.Cod.Astr. 7.238.26.

n74206.head: ὀνυχόω
n74206.html:
ὀνυχόω,

make like a nail, claw, or hook, τὸ ὠνυχωμένον the claw-shaped side of the scalpel, Orib. 46.11.18 ; ὠνύχωται has horny hoofs, Sch. Ar. Ra. 232.

n74207.head: ὀνώδης
n74207.html:
ὀνώδης, ες,

ass-like, of persons, Arist. Phgn. 812a10, Phld. Rh. 1.6 S. (Sup.); ὀ. φιλοπλουτία Plu. Cupid. 2.525e ; of colour, ib. Isid. 362f.

n74208.head: ὄνωνις
n74208.html:
ὄνωνις or ὀνωνίς, ιδος, ἡ,

rest-harrow, Ononis antiquorum, Thphr. HP 6.1.3, Dsc. 3.131 ; τρηχεῖαν ὄνωνιν Supp.Hell. fr. 1138 (ap. Plu. Aud. 2.44e, al., v.l. ἄνωνιν): metaph., ἐς [τὴν] πόλιν ἄξεις τήνδε τὴν ὀνώνιδα this troublesome weed (perh. with a play on ὄνος), Com.Adesp. 438.

n74209.head: ὀξάλειος
n74209.html:
ὀξάλειος [ᾰ], ον,

sourish, συκαῖ Apollod.Car. 25.3.

n74210.head: ὀξαλίς
n74210.html:
ὀξαλίς, ίδος, ἡ,

sour wine, Hsch.

II sorrel, Rumex acetosa, Nic. Th. 840 ; = ὀξυλάπαθον μικρόν, Ps.-Dsc. 2.114.

n74211.head: ὀξάλμη
n74211.html:
ὀξάλμη, ἡ, (ὄξος)

sauce made of vinegar and brine, Cratin. 143, Ar. V. 331 (anap.), Gal. 6.616, al.; mentioned as a natural product of Sicily, Arist. Mete. 359b15 ; used medicinally, Apollon. ap. Philum. Ven. 32.3 :—written ἐξάλμη, UPZ 89.14 (ii B. C.).

n74213.head: ὀξέλαιον
n74213.html:
ὀξέλαιον, τό,

sauce of vinegar and oil, Xenocr. ap. Orib. 2.58.119, Gal. 6.728.

n74214.head: ὀξερίας
n74214.html:
ὀξερίας, ὁ,

= τυρὸς χλωρός (Poll.) or τυρὸς ἀχρεῖος (Hsch.), name of a Sicilian cheese, Com.Adesp. 880 (fort. ξερίας).

n74215.head: ὀξηλίς
n74215.html: ὀξηλίς, ίδος, ἡ, a plant (cf. ὀξαλίς II), Theognost. Can. 14.

n74216.head: ὀξηρός
n74216.html:
ὀξηρός, ά, όν, (ὄξος)

of or for vinegar, ἄγγος S. Fr. 306 ; κεράμιον, κέραμος, Ar. Fr. 723, AP 12.108 (Dionys.) ; ἀγγεῖα Sor. 1.90.

II acid, -ῶν ἐμουμένων Diocl. Fr. 139 ; σπλῆνες ὀ. pads soaked in vinegar, Hp. Ulc. 15.

n74217.head: ὀξίδιον
n74217.html:
ὀξίδιον, τό,

Dim. of ὄξος, PCair.Zen. 527.9 (iii B. C.) : written -είδιον in Dieuch. ap. Orib. 4.7.21, Suid.: pl. ὀξείδια Sammelb. 4425 vii 20 (ii A. D.), BGU 417.31 (ii/iii A. D.).

n74218.head: ὀξίζω
n74218.html:
ὀξίζω,

taste or smell like vinegar, Dsc. 1.115.2,5.6, Gp. 3.7.1 (= interpol. in Dsc. 2.96, with -ύσῃ), Archig. ap. Gal. 13.218, etc.

corr.why: LSJ cites Archigenes fragments from Galen (Kühn vol. 13) with the standard abbreviation 'Archig. ap. Gal.'. 'Cal.' is not an LSJ abbreviation and is a C/G misreading in current. Restore Gal.

n74219.head: ὀξίνα
n74219.html:
ὀξίνα (prob. Dor. fem.),

harrow, Hsch. (Cogn. with ὀξύς, cf. Lith. ekēli, Germ. eggen ‘harrow’, Lat. occa.)

n74220.head: ὀξίνης
n74220.html:
ὀξίνης [ῐ], ου, ὁ,

sharp, sour, χυμός Plu. Aet. phys. 2.913b (codd. Wyttenb., ὀξὺν codd. Bernardak.) ; ὀξίνης (sc. οἶνος), ὁ, sour wine, Hermipp. 91, Thphr. HP 9.11.1 ; ὀ. οἶνος Hp. Vict. 2.52 (in pl. ὀξίναι), Thphr. HP 9.20.4, Diph. 82 : distd. from ὄξος, Plu. QConv. 2.732b, Stoic.rep. 1047e.

2 metaph., sour-tempered, tart, πολίτης Ar. Eq. 1304 ; θυμός Id. V. 1082.—In Gp. 6.4.2 and Phryn. PS p.92 B., we find ὄξινος :—also ὄξυνος v.l. in Gp. l.c.

n74221.head: ὀξίς
n74221.html:
ὀξίς, ίδος, ἡ, (ὄξος)

vinegar-cruet, Nicostr.Com. 9, Axionic. 7, AJA 31.351 (pl.), PLond. 2.402ii24 (ii B. C.); prop. of earthenware, Sch. Ar. Ra. 1488 : hence ὀξὶς χαλκῆ γέγονε, instead of being κεραμεᾶ, Ar. Pl. 812 ; also ὀξίδʼ ἀργυρᾶν ἔχει Sopat. 19 ; ὀξὶς ἢ φάλαγξ; (exact sense doubtful) Ar. V. 1509.

2 a measure, at Athens the same as ὀξύβαφον, but at Cleonae, = κοτύλη, Id. Fr. 688, Diph. 96.

II = ὀξαλίς II, Gal. 11.631 (where ὀξύδα).

III in pl., acidities, Alex.Trall. Febr. I: sg., acidity, ib. 6.

n74222.head: ὀξῖτις
n74222.html:
ὀξῖτις, ιδος, fem. Adj.

tasting like vinegar, στυπτηρία PHolm. 18.5, 25.39.

n74224.head: ὀξοπώλης
n74224.html:
ὀξοπώλης, ου, ὁ,

vinegar-merchant, Poll. 7.198, Lib. Or. 29.30.

n74225.head: ὄξος
n74225.html:
ὄξος, εος, τό, (ὀξύς)

poor wine, ‘vin ordinaire’, Ar. Ach. 35 ; κοτύλας τέτταρας ὄξους Δεκελικοῦ Alex. 285, cf. X. An. 2.3.14, POxy. 1275.20 (iii A. D.) ; cf. ὀξίνης I.

2 vinegar made therefrom, IG 1(2).334.4, A. Ag. 322, Hp. Acut. 61, Gal. 11.413, etc.; ὑπώμνυτο ὁ μὲν οἶνος ὄ. αὑτὸν εἶναι γνήσιον, τὸ δʼ ὄ. οἶνον αὑτό Eub. 65; σφόδρʼ ἐστὶν . . ὁ βίος οἴνῳ προσφερής· ὅταν ᾖ τὸ λοιπὸν μικρόν, ὄ. γίγνεται Antiph. 240 ; ἐς τὰς ῥῖνας ὄ. ἐγχέων, as a mode of torture, Ar. Ra. 620.

3 metaph., of a sour fellow, χὡνὴρ ὄ. ἅπαν Theoc. 15.148.

n74226.head: ὀξύα
n74226.html:
ὀξύα or ὀξύη [ῠ] (the latter preferred by Phryn. PS p.96 B. and more freq. in texts, as Thphr. HP 3.3.8, al., but ὀξύα ib. 3.10.3, 5.1.2 and 4), ἡ,

beech, Fagus silvatica, Xanth. 8, Thphr. HP 3.3.8, 3.10.1, Dicaearch. 2.2 ; later, as in Mod. Gr., called ὀξέα, Dosith. p.396 K., Gloss., condemned by Phryn. l.c.

II spear-shaft made from its wood, spear, Archil. 186, E. Heracl. 727. (Prob. cogn. with ONorse askr ‘ash’, Lat. ornus, etc.)

n74227.head: ὀξυάκανθα
n74227.html:
ὀξυάκανθα [ᾰκ], ἡ,

fiery thorn, Cotoneaster Pyracantha, Dsc. 1.93, Gal. 6.643 :—also ὀξῠ-άκανθος, Thphr. HP 1.9.3, 3.3.1, Gal. 12.90.

n74228.head: ὀξυακουσίλογος
n74228.html:
ὀξυακουσίλογος [ῐ], ον,

sharp of hearing, Lat. auritus, Gloss.

n74229.head: ὀξυαύγεια
n74229.html:
ὀξυαύγεια, ἡ,

dazzling light, Ph. Fr. 73H.

n74230.head: ὀξύβαρις
n74230.html:
ὀξύβαρις (sc. προσῳδία), ἡ,

circumflex accent, Ammonius (pupil of Aristarchus) in Gramm.Lat. 4.531 K.; called ὀξυβαρεῖα in Arc. 188.4 (spurious passage, only in cod. C).

n74231.head: ὀξυβάφιον
n74231.html:
ὀξυβάφιον [ᾰ], τό,

Dim. of sq., Antiph. 163.5, POxy. 1657.7 (iii A.D.) ; -βάφια τρύλλια Stud.Pal. 20.67.10 (ii A.D.).

n74232.head: ὀξύβαφον
n74232.html:
ὀξύβαφον, τό, (βάπτω)

small vinegar-saucer : then, generally, shallow earthen vessel, saucer, Hp. Morb. 2.47, Cratin. 187, Ar. Av. 361, Antiph. 163.5 (v.l.), Eub. 65, Inscr.Délos 407.18 (ii B.C.), etc.

2 pl., a kind of harmonica made of saucers of different materials struck with a wooden hammer, Phlp. in de An. 353.13 (ὀψόβ- codd.), Suid. s.v. Διοκλῆς.

II as a measure, the fourth part of a κοτύλη, about 1/8 of a pint, μέλιτος Alex. 172.11, cf. Thphr. HP 9.11.7, al., Nic. Th. 598, Dsc. 3.27. (The form ὀξόβαφον BGU 781 iii 5 (i A.D.), PMed.Strassb. p.7 K., is condemned by Phryn. PS p.97 B.)

n74233.head: ὀξυβελής
n74233.html:
ὀξυβελής, ές,

sharp-pointed, ἆλτο δʼ ὀϊστὸς ὀξυβελής Il. 4.126 ; ὀ. χαῖται, of the porcupineʼs bristles, Emp. 83.2 ; ἥλιος Id. 40 ; νῶτα καράβου Opp. H. 2.346 : metaph., πόθος ὀ. ib. 4.41 : in Prose, of a lancet, τὸ -ές Gal. 12.413.

II shooting sharp-pointed, and therefore swift, missiles, ὀ. [ὄργανα], opp. λιθοβολικά, Ph. Bel. 54.49 ; ὀξυβελής, ὁ, with and without καταπέλτης, an engine for throwing sharp-pointed bolts, opp. πετροβόλος, D.S. 20.85, 86 ; so ὀξυβελικόν (sc. ὄργανον), τό, ib. 75, etc.

n74234.head: ὀξύβλαττα
n74234.html:
ὀξύβλαττα, ἡ, (ὀξύς II.2b)

in Lat. form oxyblatta, bright purple, Cod.Just. 4.40.1.

n74235.head: ὀξυβλεπτέω
n74235.html:
ὀξυβλεπτέω,

to be sharp-sighted, Arr. Epict. 2.11.22.

n74236.head: ὀξυβλέπτης
n74236.html:
ὀξυβλέπτης, ου, ὁ,

one who is sharp-sighted, Hsch. s.v. ἀτρέστοις, Gloss.

n74237.head: ὀξυβλεψία
n74237.html:
ὀξυβλεψία, ἡ,

sharpness of sight, Hsch. s.v. ὀξυωπίαν.

n74238.head: ὀξυβόας
n74238.html:
ὀξυβόας and ὀξῠ-βόης, ου, ὁ,

shrill-screaming, of birds, A. Ag. 57 ; of men, Luc. JTr. 31 ; sharp-buzzing, of mosquitoes, AP 5.150 (Mel.).

n74239.head: ὀξυβόλος
n74239.html:
ὀξυβόλος, ον,

= ὀξυβελής II, IG 2(2).468 (iv B.C.).

n74240.head: ὀξυβουλία
n74240.html:
ὀξυβουλία, ἡ,

quickness of counsel, Sch.B Il. 10.204 (better ὀξυλαβία, as Sch.T).

n74241.head: ὀξυβρέχω
n74241.html:
ὀξυβρέχω,

steep in vinegar, Stud.Pal. 20.27.2 (ii/iii A.D.).

n74242.head: ὀξύγαλα
n74242.html:
ὀξύγαλα, ακτος, τό,

sour milk, whey, πίνουσι . . ὀ. τῶν προβάτων Ctes. Fr. 57.22, cf. Str. 7.4.6, Plu. Art. 3, Gal. 6.689.

n74243.head: ὀξυγαλάκτινος
n74243.html:
ὀξυγαλάκτινος, η, ον,

made of sour milk, τυρός Gal. 6.697, 12.272, cf. 6.518.

n74244.head: ὀξύγαρον
n74244.html:
ὀξύγαρον, τό,

sauce of vinegar and γάρον, Arr. Epict. 2.20.30, Gal. 6.534, Ath. 2.67e, 9.366c:—also ὀξόγαρον, Gloss., condemned by Phryn. PS p.97 B.
n74244.gloss: a sauce of vinegar and fish sauce

n74245.head: ὀξύγγιον
n74245.html:
ὀξύγγιον, τό,

= Lat. axungia, lard, Dsc. 3.90, al., Orib. Fr. 97, Gloss.

n74246.head: ὀξυγένειος
n74246.html:
ὀξυγένειος, ον,

with pointed chin, Poll. 4.145.

n74247.head: ὀξύγενυς
n74247.html:
ὀξύγενυς, υος, ὁ,

point of the chin, Poll. 2.97.

n74248.head: ὀξύγη
n74248.html:
ὀξύγη, ἡ,

= εἶδος <ἀ>κρίδος, Lat. bufo et cufo, Gloss.

n74249.head: ὀξύγλυκυ
n74249.html:
ὀξύγλυκυ (sc. ποτόν), τό,

drink of acidulated honey, Hp. Fract. 11 (in dat. -εῖ), 36 (in acc. -υ), etc. :—so ὀξυ-γλῠκές, τό, Gal. 18(2).466 ; ὀξύ-γλῠκον, τό, Lat. dulcacidum, Gloss.

n74250.head: ὀξύγλυκυς
n74250.html:
ὀξύγλυκυς, εια, υ,

sour-sweet, ῥόα A. Fr. 363 ; ὁ τῆς ὀξυγλύκεος ῥοιᾶς χυλός (prob. a special variety) Orib. Fr. 53.

n74251.head: ὀξύγονον
n74251.html:
ὀξύγονον, τό,

= μήκων ῥοιάς, cj. in Ps.-Dsc. 4.63,64 (-τονον codd., cf. Apul. Herb. 53, Gloss.).

n74252.head: ὀξύγοος
n74252.html:
ὀξύγοος, ον,

shrill-wailing, λιταί A. Th. 320 (lyr.).

n74253.head: ὀξυγράφος
n74253.html:
ὀξυγράφος [ᾰ], ον,

writing fast, LXX Ps. 44 (45). 2, Ph. 2.363, etc.

n74254.head: ὀξυγώνιος
n74254.html:
ὀξυγώνιος, ον,

acute-angled, Arist. Top. 107a17, Cael. 307a2, Euc. 1Def. 21, Onos. 10.16 : neut. as Subst., acute-angled body, Epicur. Ep. 2 p.50 U. (pl.).

n74255.head: ὀξυγωνιότης
n74255.html:
ὀξυγωνιότης, ητος, ἡ,

a being acute-angled, Apollod. Poliorc. 159.7.

n74256.head: ὀξυδερκέω
n74256.html: ὀξυδερκέω, prob. f.l. for ὀξυδορκέω, Ph. 1.409, 2.480, Hsch. s.v. ἐκ δυοῖν τρία βλέπεις (-δορκ- Suid.).

n74257.head: ὀξυδερκής
n74257.html:
ὀξυδερκής, ές,

sharp-sighted, quick-sighted, Luc. Tim. 25, al. : Comp. -έστερος Id. Vit.Auct. 26, Hegesand. 9 ; ὄψις Alex.Aphr. in Top. 262.10 : Sup. -έστατος Hdt. 2.68, Arist. Mir. 834b28. Adv. -κῶς Ph. 1.590 : Comp. -έστερον ib. 229.

II Act., promoting quickness of sight, ὕδωρ Diocl. Fr. 128, cf. Dsc. 5.5, Gal. 12.263, al.

n74258.head: ὀξυδερκία
n74258.html:
ὀξυδερκία, ἡ,

sharp-sightedness, αἰσθήσεων Epicur. Nat. 28Fr. 6, cf. Apollod. 3.10.3, Gal. 14.241, Alex.Aphr. in Top. 258.17, etc.: Ion. ὀξυ-δερκείη Democr. 119.

n74259.head: ὀξυδερκικός
n74259.html:
ὀξυδερκικός, ή, όν,

making the sight sharp, as L. Dind. for ὀξυδερκιῶν in Antyll. ap. Orib. 10.23.29 (ὀξυδορκικῶν Dar.) ; -δερκικοῖς (and -δορκικοῖς) v.l. for -δερκέσι in Dsc. 2.163.

n74260.head: ὀξυδερκώ
n74260.html: ὀξυδερκώ, οῦς, ἡ, epith. of Athena, Paus. 2.24.2.

n74261.head: ὀξυδορκέω
n74261.html:
ὀξυδορκέω,

to be quick of sight, Arist. Rh.Al. 1421a22, Com.Adesp. 359, Str. 6.2.1, etc.; v. -δερκέω.

n74262.head: ὀξυδορκία
n74262.html:
ὀξυδορκία, ἡ,

= ὀξυδερκία, Andronic.Rhod. p. 572 M., Hippod. ap. Stob. 4.39.26, Plot. 5.9.1, etc.

n74263.head: ὀξυδορκικός
n74263.html:
ὀξυδορκικός, ή, όν,

= ὀξυδερκικός (q.v.), Plu. Adul. 2.69a, Gal. 11.778.

n74264.head: ὀξύδουπος
n74264.html:
ὀξύδουπος, ον,

sharp-sounding, κύμβαλα AP 6.94 (Phil.).

n74265.head: ὀξυδρόμος
n74265.html:
ὀξυδρόμος, ον,

swift-running, Sch. Pi. O. 13.51.

n74266.head: ὀξυέθειρ
n74266.html:
ὀξυέθειρ, gen. -έθειρος, ὁ, ἡ,

with sharp points, nom. pl. -έθειρες, ἐχῖνοι Marc.Sid. 35 ; acc. pl. -έθειρας, ἀκάνθας Nonn. D. 14.368 ; gen.sg. -έθειρος, ἀκάνθης ib. 22.25.

n74267.head: ὀξυέλαιον
n74267.html:
ὀξυέλαιον, τό,

mixture of oil and vinegar, Gal. 13.397.

n74268.head: ὀξυζύμια
n74268.html:
ὀξυζύμια [ῡ], τά,

acid ferments, Ps.-Democr. ap. Zos.Alch. p.160 B.

n74270.head: ὀξύζωμος
n74270.html:
ὀξύζωμος, ον,

with a sharp sauce, Apic. 6.9.241.

n74272.head: ὀξυηκοΐα
n74272.html:
ὀξυηκοΐα, Dor. ὀξυ-ᾱκοΐα, ἡ,

a sharp, quick ear, Hippod. ap. Stob. 4.39.26, Metop. ib. 3.1.115, Plu. Aud.poet. 2.34c, Alex.Aphr. in Top. 327.14, interpol. in Poll. 2.82.

n74273.head: ὀξυήκοος
n74273.html:
ὀξυήκοος, ον,

quick of hearing : of quick perception, keen, αἴσθησις Pl. Ti. 75b ; ἰχθύες Arist. HA 534a6, cf. A.D. Synt. 295.23.—In codd. sts. wrongly ὀξύκοος, ὀξυκοΐα : Comp. ὀξυηκοώτερος Luc. Pr.Im. 20, Porph. Abst. 3.8 : Sup. ὀξυηκοώτατος prob. l. in S.E. M. 9.65, for ὀξυηκούστατος.

n74274.head: ὀξυηχής
n74274.html:
ὀξυηχής, ές,

sharp-sounding, of high notes, Philostr. VS 1.8.1 :

n74276.head: ὀξυθανασία
n74276.html:
ὀξυθανασία, ἡ,

early death, Heliod.Astr. in Cat.Cod.Astr. 8(4).238.

n74277.head: ὀξυθάνατος
n74277.html:
ὀξυθάνατος [θᾰ], ον,

dying quickly, short-lived, Eun. Hist. p.269 D., Heliod.Astr. in Cat.Cod.Astr. 4.154.

II killing quickly, Str. 17.2.4 (Comp.).
